description_en: A Śivaśikharatemple from approx. 14th-15th.The temple is located within the Jagannātha temple complex, 1,5 kilometres south-east from Chipur. A few meters to the east the temple flows the Jagannātha Kholā.The temple is built in thelatina nāgaramode. The door of the temple is oriented to the south-west. It is preceded by a 13 meters long hall (bhoga maṇḍapa). This is a later addition. The interior of both the hall and the temple could not be surveyed during the site's visit. The north-western, north-eastern and south-eastern façades each contain a niche. A broken stone statue of a lion is in placed in the south-eastern niche. The lion was most probably originally placed on top of the temple's pediment (śukanāsikā).On top of theśikharais anāmalakadisc. The whole upper part of the temple is covered by a hip roof with metal sheets (?), supported by wooden pillars. This covering is very similar to that of temples found in north-western India.Dedicated to Jagannāth, the temple was dated from the 12th century by D. R. Sharma (Sharma 2012, p. 288-289), although a later dating, from the 14th-15th century may also be proposed.
monument_assessment: Good (very few light surface damages, renovated or repaired)
references: REFERENCES Sharma, Dilli Raj. 2012. Heritage of Western Nepal. Art and Architecture . Kathmandu: Centre for Nepal and Asian Studies.
